title: A spiral that draws itself
view: central 768^2 cells of a 1024^2 periodic world, 1 px per cell, fixed camera
caveats: Catalogued species and catalogued behaviour: Chan 2019 sec. 3.5.4 (pdf p. 28) describes 'spiral elongation (in Helicidae)' with quadratic mass growth. Nothing here is new; the exhibit shows ALM reproducing it at a large world size.

Single run, alm only. In a 512^2 world (G012) the arm meets its own periodic image by about 70 tu and a labyrinth texture takes over where it collides. This film uses a 1024^2 world, stops at 150 tu and shows only the central 768^2 cells.

runs.initial_state: catalog entry #197 (HN+m Catenohelicium monospirae) cells placed centred on zero 1024^2 (VIS-talk survey.place)

render.colormap: matplotlib inferno, A in [0,1] mapped linearly, nearest-neighbour

reproduce: git checkout <this commit> && .venv/bin/python research/experiments/VIS-talk/film.py G013   # verify only: film.py verify G013
